newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. envoy meets Masood in northern Afghan town.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy meets Masood in northern Afghan town.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Norbert Holl met ousted government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood on Sunday for the first time since the Taleban militia captured Kabul on September 27, U.N. sources said.

The talks, in the northern city of Kunduz, focused on U.N. proposals for a ceasefire, a joint commission to supervise it, demilitarisation of Kabul, formation of a neutral Afghan police force and a direct dialogue between the warring parties.
The sources said Masood agreed in principle to the proposals and told Holl he would nominate his representatives for a dialogue with the radical Islamic Taleban militia.
They said the peace dialogue could start soon in an unidentified neutral country. A technical committee would be set up to work in parallel with the main political talks.

Holl planned to visit the southern city of Kandahar for talks with senior Taleban leaders on Tuesday and the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Thursday to meet Masood's ally General Abdul Rashid Dostum, the sources said.
The Taleban's acting Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammed Ghous indicated in a meeting with Holl two days ago that the movement was ready to start direct talks with its foes, the sources said.
Forces of Masood and Dostum have been battling the Taleban north of Kabul and in northwest Afghanistan since the fall of the capital, but neither side has gained a clear advantage.
